description:
Found in defk-l2g (2026-10-15, provisional, load 4-7). With Myers bit-parallel Levenshtein, fuzzy_search's kernel spends ~4 ms per query over 234k words, a few ns per word. The fast-path report says of the word loop: 'loop: a safepoint every iteration: the body has a nested loop'. The inner Enum.reduce_while over the word's bytes runs in strips, charged on entry. bench/yield_cost.exs: yielding 4.9 ms vs yield: false 4.1-4.2 ms, +19%, at ~17 yields per query; with the DP kernel it was +3.5-4.5%. A huge slice (DEFK_SLICE_US=10000000) did not change the yields or the gap, so the cost is the per-word bookkeeping, not the yields. Under load defk serves ~21% fewer req/s than the blocking build (1790-1840 vs 2260-2370).

Scope: find what the per-iteration safepoint of an outer loop with a short inner loop costs (the check, the resume dispatch, registers kept live; compare defk-w8l), and try a cheaper shape, for example charging the outer loop in strips by the inner loop's trip count, or one safepoint per N outer iterations. Keep the worst-case scheduler gap within the slice. Record the result in docs/performance.md and re-run examples/fuzzy_search/bench/yield_cost.exs.

Done when: the breakdown is recorded and either a fix lands with mix test green and the fuzzy_search yield cost re-measured, or the ticket records why no fix was worth it.

comments.text: Merged into defk-w8l on 2026-10-20: both tickets are the per-iteration yield bookkeeping of short loops, and defk-w8l already cited the fuzzy_search case. The evidence and scope of this ticket are now in defk-w8l's description.

title: A word loop whose body holds a short inner loop pays a safepoint per word: fuzzy_search Myers yields +19% over yield: false
